findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the emitter's decision rule that turns sidecar absence into a valid `expect: pass` no-fire case (require the criterion to have been in-cohort/routed for that plan AND to have produced zero findings), and state how rows lacking a cohort key are handled.
evidence: plan_review/sidecar.py:649-717 `_slim` persists a per-FINDING record; a criterion that produced no finding leaves no row, so 'stayed silent' is an ABSENCE inference
The emitted artifact shape (src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/plan-review-necessity.eval.yaml) requires explicit `expect: pass` no-fire cases, not just `expect: finding` cases

sidecar.py:667-672 cohort comment: a finding 'written before this field (or by a path that doesn't stamp it) has NO cohort key' — so which criteria were in-cohort (routed) for a given plan is itself only partially recoverable

ABSENCE rationale: the plan never states the predicate that qualifies a sidecar row as a valid no-fire case (criterion in-cohort AND zero findings), so an executor cannot deterministically emit expect:pass cases
findings.finding: The emitter's rule for producing a no-fire (expect: pass) fixture case from the sidecar corpus is unspecified: the sidecar records only findings that FIRED, so a criterion 'staying silent' on a plan cannot be distinguished from a criterion that was never routed/in-cohort on that plan without an explicit decision rule the plan does not state.
findings.location: Context / Problem ('enough to state, for a real plan, which criteria fired and which stayed silent') and Approach ('per-criterion fire/no-fire eval fixtures')
scenarios: A criterion silent on a plan only because chunking never routed it to that criterion gets emitted as an expect:pass case; a later rubric edit that (correctly) fires on that plan is then scored as a false-fire regression against a fixture that never encoded real behavior
The emitter cannot decide which real plans are eligible no-fire evidence, blocking the Coverage AC for criteria whose corpus evidence is entirely silence
findings.suggested_fix: Define a no-fire predicate in the selector/emitter: a plan is admissible no-fire evidence for criterion C only if C is present in that row's `cohort` (routed/evaluated) and no finding cites C; rows with a MISSING cohort key are skipped as no-fire candidates (never emitted as expect:pass).

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Assign ownership of the AC1 completeness verifier script (routing set vs. .rebar/evals + eval_specs + open unreliable-criterion: titles, exit non-zero on a gap) to one child with an AC that runs it green.
evidence: Parent AC1 names a specific verification artifact: a script comparing the routing key set to the evals dirs and open-ticket titles.

Selector ACs assert manifest rows/reasons; emitter ACs assert emitted specs; admission ACs assert admitted/withheld/drift; self-healing ACs assert ticket creation and gap selection — none assert the union-completeness exit-non-zero script.
Absence rationale: searched every sibling's indented ACs in the roster; no criterion measures the same observable outcome (the completeness exit code).
findings.finding: No child owns the AC1 verifier script itself. AC1 is stated as 'verified by a script that sets the routing key set against ls .rebar/evals/ src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/ and the open-ticket titles, and exits non-zero if any criterion is in neither set.' No sibling's acceptance criteria deliver that script or that exit-code assertion; the children only produce specs, tickets, and reports.
scenarios: At epic sign-off nobody runs a check that every uncovered criterion is in exactly one of {has-spec, has-unreliable-ticket}; the invariant is asserted only by the parent verifier, which no child builds or exercises.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the verifier script and a passing AC to either the admission runner or the self-healing child.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Ensure a criterion that fails reproduction or is skipped-unbalanced during the epic's admission pass has an open unreliable-criterion: ticket (or spec) at epic close, so AC1's completeness verifier can pass without waiting for three self-healing intervals.
evidence: Parent AC1: 'either has a spec file under .rebar/evals/, or an open ticket titled unreliable-criterion: <criterion-id> ... exits non-zero if any criterion is in neither set.'
67aa disposition: 'A candidate that does not reproduce is withheld from the suite and written to a drift report' — no ticket is filed by the admission runner.
1cef circuit breaker: 'On the third such run it creates a ticket titled exactly unreliable-criterion: <criterion-id>' and its trigger 'default[s] to 30 days.'

Parent decomposition claims residual gaps are 'handled by the self-healing loop, which files the unreliable-criterion: tickets' — but that filing is gated on three interval-spaced runs, not on epic completion.
findings.finding: Parent AC1's completeness invariant is not satisfied at epic close for a criterion whose candidates fail to reproduce in the admission run: that criterion gets no spec (67aa withholds it) and no unreliable-criterion: ticket, because the ticket is only filed by the self-healing loop after THREE consecutive failed runs at a 30-day default interval. The AC1 verifier (exits non-zero if any criterion is in neither the evals set nor the open-ticket-title set) would therefore fail right after the epic's admission run is committed.
scenarios: A criterion with real candidates that all disagree with current code: admission run withholds it; no ticket exists; the AC1 completeness script exits non-zero at epic sign-off.
A criterion reported skipped-unbalanced in the epic's single emitter/admission pass: same — no spec, no ticket, until three self-healing runs elapse.
findings.suggested_fix: Give the admission runner (67aa) an AC that files the unreliable-criterion: ticket (or an equivalent recorded row) for any criterion left with neither a spec nor an existing ticket at the end of the bootstrap run, or add an explicit reconciliation/verifier step owned by one child that satisfies AC1 at epic close.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the selector/emitter fallback for plan_review_result_v1 rows that lack the v2 lossless fields (evidence/scenarios/decision_margin/block_threshold): whether v1 rows are excluded from candidate selection or handled with a documented degraded path.
evidence: corpus-2026-08-30.manifest.json schema_histogram: plan_review_result_v1 = 1833, plan_review_result_v2 = 4649 (row_count 6482)
sidecar.py:654-657: 'Story 4e19 makes the record LOSSLESS (v2): the Pass-1 evidence/scenarios grounding prose is now persisted too, along with the resolved block_threshold/blocking_enabled'
sidecar.py:703-705: decision_margin added in 'story fixable-angular-caribou', 'None when either side is absent → offline readers treat a missing margin as unknown'

ABSENCE rationale: the plan names decision_margin as load-bearing candidate-selection evidence but never states what the selector does with the ~28% of rows (v1) whose grounding/margin fields are absent
findings.finding: The plan treats decision_margin (and the lossless evidence/scenarios grounding) as uniformly available across the corpus, but those fields are v2-only additions and 1,833 of 6,482 rows are the older plan_review_result_v1 schema; the plan specifies no fallback for candidates mined from v1 rows that lack these fields.
findings.location: Context / Problem ('sidecar.py:650-716 retains, per finding, the `criteria` list, `norm_id`, `decision`, and `decision_margin`')
scenarios: The selector reads decision_margin/evidence on a v1 row, gets None/empty, and either silently drops otherwise-good candidates or emits a fixture with no grounding prose
Coverage AC counts a criterion as evidence-less because all its corpus rows happen to be v1, when the real cause is a schema gap the plan didn't account for
findings.suggested_fix: Add an explicit rule: candidate selection considers only plan_review_result_v2 rows (or documents a v1 degraded path that omits margin-based ranking), and correct the Context claim that sidecar.py:650-716 uniformly retains decision_margin — it is v2-only.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the admission runner (67aa) accept caller-supplied cap_usd and ledger_path so the self-healing loop (1cef) can drive it at $25 against its own ledger without duplicating admission logic.
evidence: 1cef: 'It reuses the sibling selector, emitter and admission runner rather than duplicating any of them' and 'Each run pre-flights through ledger.reserve(..., cap_usd=25.0) against the loop's own ledger file.'

67aa: 'The run pre-flights through ledger.reserve(..., cap_usd=250.0) using the parameterized ledger from the sibling ledger child, against this epic's own ledger file' — cap and path given as fixed to 250.0 and the epic ledger.
67aa file_impact ledger path is docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/fixtures/ledger.jsonl; 1cef adds 'a new ledger file' — two different files, but the reused runner is described as bound to the first.
findings.finding: Conflicting assumption / dependency gap between the self-healing loop (1cef) and the admission runner (67aa) over the admission runner's budget cap and ledger path. 1cef 'reuses the sibling ... admission runner' but must drive it at cap_usd=25.0 against 'the loop's own ledger file', while 67aa describes the admission runner as pre-flighting ledger.reserve(..., cap_usd=250.0) against 'this epic's own ledger file' with those values stated as fixed, not caller-supplied. The runner is not stated to accept a caller-provided cap or ledger path.
scenarios: The self-healing loop invokes the admission runner and expects a $25 cap on its own ledger, but the runner enforces $250 on the epic ledger — the $25/interval unattended bound is not actually enforced through the reused code path.
Self-healing spend lands in the epic's admission ledger, or the runner refuses at the wrong ceiling.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an AC to 67aa exposing the admission entry point with parameterized cap_usd and ledger_path (defaulting to 250.0 and the epic ledger), and have 1cef pass 25.0 and its own ledger file.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Pin distinct, named ledger-file paths for the admission runner and the self-healing loop (or explicitly state they share one) so the $25/interval and $250 caps compose without a shared-spend collision.
evidence: 67aa: pre-flights 'against this epic's own ledger file' (docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/fixtures/ledger.jsonl).
1cef: pre-flights 'against the loop's own ledger file' and Compatibility notes 'a new ledger file.'
fb55 context: '_spent_so_far sums only the rows of the file it is handed' — a shared file means shared spend accounting.
findings.finding: Ledger-file identity between the admission runner and the self-healing loop is ambiguous, creating a potential implicit-shared-state hazard. If 'this epic's own ledger file' (67aa) and 'the loop's own ledger file' (1cef) resolve to the same path, the self-healing loop's cap_usd=25.0 reserve would immediately raise BudgetExceeded against the admission run's already-recorded ~$112 spend, since ledger.reserve sums existing rows in the handed file.
scenarios: If both children write the same ledger.jsonl, the first self-healing run is refused because prior epic spend already exceeds $25.
If they are intentionally separate, the parent's $450 aggregate ceiling is enforced only as disjoint per-file caps, not as one ceiling.
findings.suggested_fix: State the self-healing loop's ledger path explicitly (distinct from the admission runner's) in both 1cef and the parent budget section.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Clarify whether AC4's 'epic ceiling' is the aggregate $450 (needing a shared accounting) or per-child caps summing to $450; if aggregate, assign an owner that refuses on the summed spend.
evidence: Parent Budget: 'Epic ceiling $450 including a $75 reserve, enforced by the parameterized ledger.'
Parent AC4: 'exceed the epic ceiling is refused before it issues any model call.'
fb55 tests refusal at parameterized caps (e.g., 50/10, 200/30); 67aa tests refusal at its 250 reserve — neither tests a $450 aggregate.
Parent Non-goals of fb55: 'Any shared or global budget registry spanning epics' is explicitly out of scope, so no cross-child aggregate ceiling exists by design.
findings.finding: No child enforces the parent's stated aggregate epic ceiling of $450 as a single refusal boundary. AC4 says 'A run whose pre-flight estimate would exceed the epic ceiling is refused before it issues any model call.' The children enforce only per-child caps (admission 250, self-healing 25) against separate ledger files; nothing refuses when the SUM across children approaches $450.
scenarios: The admission runner, self-healing runs, and change-triggered runs each clear their own per-file pre-flight but jointly exceed $450 over the epic's life; no refusal fires because no ledger observes the aggregate.
findings.suggested_fix: Either restate AC4 to reference the composed per-child caps ($250+$100+$25+reserve) verified individually, or add a child/AC that enforces the $450 aggregate before any model call.
